quiz.title: ISC Class 12 Maths Sample Paper Quiz
quiz.intro: Eight questions sampling the ISC Class 12 syllabus — calculus, probability, vectors and 3D, conics, linear regression and matrices. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.

questions.q: What is the value of ∫ from 0 to 1 of 2x dx?
questions.explanation: ∫ 2x dx = x². Evaluated from 0 to 1 gives 1² − 0² = 1.

questions.q: A fair die is rolled once. What is the probability of getting a number greater than 4?
questions.explanation: Numbers greater than 4 are 5 and 6, so 2 favourable outcomes out of 6, which is 2/6 = 1/3.

questions.q: If a = i + 2j + 2k, what is its magnitude |a|?
The eccentricity of the ellipse x²/25 + y²/16 = 1 is:
questions.explanation: Here a² = 25, b² = 16, so e = √(1 − b²/a²) = √(1 − 16/25) = √(9/25) = 3/5.

questions.q: For the two regression lines, the coefficient of correlation r is the ___ of the two regression coefficients (with the sign of the coefficients).
questions.explanation: r = ±√(b_yx · b_xy), the geometric mean of the two regression coefficients, taking the common sign of b_yx and b_xy.

questions.q: What is the determinant of the 2×2 matrix [[3, 4], [1, 2]]?
questions.explanation: For [[a, b], [c, d]] the determinant is ad − bc = (3)(2) − (4)(1) = 6 − 4 = 2.

questions.q: What is the derivative of sin(x²) with respect to x?
questions.explanation: By the chain rule, d/dx sin(u) = cos(u)·u' with u = x², so the answer is 2x cos(x²).

faq.q: What topics do ISC Class 12 Maths sample papers cover?
faq.a: They span the full ISC syllabus — calculus (differentiation, integration, differential equations), probability, vectors and three-dimensional geometry, conic sections, linear regression, and matrices and determinants. Section A is compulsory, with a choice between Section B (vectors/3D/conics) and Section C (linear regression/applications).

faq.q: How is the ISC Class 12 Maths paper structured?
faq.a: The theory paper is 80 marks over three hours. Section A carries 65 marks and is compulsory; you then attempt either Section B or Section C for the remaining 15 marks. The other 20 marks come from the project work.

faq.q: How many sample papers should I solve before the exam?
faq.a: Aim for at least 8 to 10 full papers under timed conditions in the last two months. Solving fewer papers slowly, then reviewing every mistake, beats rushing through twenty without checking your working.

faq.q: Should I focus more on Section B or Section C?
faq.a: Pick based on your strength. Most students find Section B (vectors, 3D geometry, conics) more scoring if their geometry is solid, while Section C (linear regression, application of calculus in commerce) suits those comfortable with statistics. Practise both early, then commit to one.
